newsitem.title: USA: PG&E to acquire Valero in $1.5 billion deal.
newsitem.headline: PG&E to acquire Valero in $1.5 billion deal.

text.p: PG&E Corp. Friday said it plans to merge with Valero Energy Corp. and acquire its natural gas services business in a deal valued at $1.5 billion.
PG&E said the acquisition will not include Valero's wholly owned subsidiary, Valero Refining and Marketing Co., which will be spun off prior to the merger.

Valero Natural Gas Co.'s operations include transporting and marketing natural gas and natural gas liquids and the marketing of electric power. The company's pipeline system has the capacity to transport more than 3 billion cubic feet of gas a day.

PG&E said it will acquire Valero for about $1.5 billion, plus adjustments for working capital and other considerations. PG&E will issue $722.5 million of common stock, in exchange for outstanding shares of Valero common stock, and will assume some debt and other liabilities.

Each Valero shareholder will receive about 0.63 shares of PG&E common stock for each Valero share, based on a PG&E closing price Thursday of $22.75 per share. The value to Valero shareholders is about $14.25 per share of Valero stock. The merger is expected to be completed by mid-1997.

Valero's shareholders also will receive one share of the spun-off refining and marketing company. The new refining and marketing company will retain the Valero name and will apply to be listed on the New York Stock Exchange. Both the spin-off of the refining and marketing business and the merger with a subsidiary of PG&E Corp. are expected to be tax-free transactions for Valero shareholders.
